title: burst-detector-hash-collision-causes-tenant-quota-misattribution-and-429-surge-action-plan
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 between 14:02–14:38 UTC we experienced a multi-tenant 429 surge affecting traffic through the egress proxy cluster in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Root cause analysis shows a collision in the gateway's tenant hashing that was introduced by a deterministic-hash optimization shipped in proxy v2.3.1. When requests contained a large number of headers (>8KB serialized), the hash reducer truncated entropy in a way that caused unrelated tokens/keys to collapse into the same quota bucket. That misattribution was amplified by the new quota-enforcer LRU trimming change, allowing a small subset of busy tenants to consume multiple buckets on behalf of others. The combination led to sudden quota exhaustion signals and widespread 429 responses for many tenants, surface-level symptom seen as a storm of client retries and elevated error budgets across customer-facing services.

What went wrong (high-level):
- A deterministic-hash micro-optimization (proxy v2.3.1) reduced bucket entropy for long-header requests, increasing collision risk.
- Quota-enforcer LRU trimming (enforcer v1.9) held a small set of keys longer than intended after the hash reducer change, enabling cross-tenant misattribution.
- Rate detector logic treated the collision as a single tenant burst, triggering backpressure and global enforcement instead of isolating to the true origin.
- Canary/rollout telemetry did not include a long-header path synthetic that would have caught the regression.

Impact:
- Multiple paying customers saw elevated 429 rates for 36 minutes; a small number of clients reported application-level failures and support tickets.
- Latency and error budgets for RPC layers spiked in affected regions; on-call paging and manual mitigations were required.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
- Rolled back proxy v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (14:20–14:40 UTC) to restore previous hashing behavior.
- Applied a temporary rule in the quota-enforcer to ignore collisions detected by identical byte-length + prefix heuristics (14:25 UTC).
- Opened emergency support threads and provided customers with a status note and mitigation ETA.

Primary action plan (this ticket):
1) Fix: Revert the deterministic-hash reducer and implement a safe hashing fallback that preserves entropy for requests with large header sets. (owner: ENG-networking)
2) Fix: Modify quota-enforcer to namespace buckets by full tenant id + stable nonce and harden LRU eviction to prefer oldest lease, not most-recently-seen. (owner: ENG-enforcer)
3) Test: Add synthetic canaries covering long-header and high-entropy header shapes to the CI canary suite and add a smoke test that asserts per-tenant quota separation. (owner: ENG-sre)
4) Observability: Add an explicit metric for "quota_bucket_collision_rate" with dimensions region, proxy_version, and header_size_bucket and dashboard + alert (>0.5% sustained over 1m). (owner: ENG-observability)
5) Rollout: Ship fixes behind feature flag; perform progressive canary by traffic-shape (normal headers -> long headers) and region (eu->us) with 30m hold window. (owner: ENG-release)
6) Post-incident runbook: Document manual diagnostics and mitigation steps for similar misattribution cases and update on-call playbook. (owner: ENG-ops)

Success criteria:
- No collisions observed in canary metrics for 1 week after rollout.
- No repeat customer 429 incidents on same vectors for 90 days.
- New tests pass in CI and synthetic canaries run every 15 minutes.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident timeline dashboard: https://dash.reedwood.internal/d/incident/ENG-58212-2026-03-09
- Root cause PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4123
- Emergency rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4127
- Support incident thread: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2026-03-09-gateway-429

Notes on uniqueness: This incident differs from prior quota/429 incidents due to the intersection of a hashing micro-optimization and LRU eviction semantics. Previous work tracked quota propagation, clock drift and token-routing — this is a collision-induced misattribution that surfaces only under specific header shapes and new hash semantics.
